cim: US federal prosecutors say businesses have lost $129M+ to scam calls using AI-generated voices to mimic company executives in the 18 months since July 2024 (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)
cim_eredeti: US federal prosecutors say businesses have lost $129M+ to scam calls using AI-generated voices to mimic company executives in the 18 months since July 2024 (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)
szoveg_eredeti:
An accountant at a regional hospital system in Missouri answering the phone recognized the voice on the other end as that of the organization’s chief executive.

There was an urgent matter that required confidentiality and an immediate wire transfer, the caller said. A lawyer then quickly followed up to complete the transaction.

By the time the hospital’s actual executives realized what had happened, $4.8 million had vanished.

The executive and the lawyer never made the calls; instead, both voices had been generated by artificial intelligence, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

The same script played out several times over approximately 18 months, beginning in July 2024, prosecutors said, costing companies based in the United States and Europe more than $129 million.

Attempts were also made to engage employees in video calls, deploying deepfakes of the chief executive in the scheme, prosecutors said.

Among the unnamed victims were: a British financial technology company ($11.6 million); a pet food company in Florida ($5 million); a hospital system in California ($3 million); a mutual fund company in Massachusetts ($4.7 million); and a bank based in Rhode Island ($2.7 million).
